title: Solve it: a morning schedule in order
idea: GUIDED PROBLEM. Report a schedule where the ORDER of the facts is the whole point. Emphasizes output order as a decision, not an accident.
problem: Show a morning schedule, each step on its own line and in the right order: wake up, eat breakfast, brush teeth.

exercises.prompt:
PROBLEM: Show a morning schedule in order — wake up, eat breakfast, brush teeth.

What is the OUTPUT?
options: Three lines showing the steps in the right order
exercises.explanation: The output is the three steps, each on its own line, in the correct order.

exercises.prompt: In a schedule, the order of the lines matters.
exercises.explanation: Yes — a schedule read out of order would be wrong. Order is part of the correct output.

exercises.prompt: Example. Work out the correct output by hand — put the real-life steps in the order they happen.
exercises.explanation: You wake up, then eat, then brush. That real-life order is the output you must match.

exercises.prompt: Plan: how do you make the computer show the steps in that exact order?
options: Write the print lines in that same order, top to bottom
Write them in any order — it sorts itself
Use one print for all three
exercises.explanation: The computer runs lines top to bottom, so writing them in order is the plan.

exercises.prompt: Plan check: the computer will reorder your lines to make sense on its own.
exercises.explanation: It will not. The computer shows lines in the exact order you write them — ordering is your job.

exercises.prompt: Code. Arrange the print lines to match the schedule order.
exercises.explanation: wake up, then eat breakfast, then brush teeth — matching the plan and the hand example.

exercises.prompt: Build the first schedule line (it should show wake up).
exercises.explanation: print("wake up") shows the whole phrase, spaces and all, on one line.

exercises.prompt:
Check. The output is:

wake up
eat breakfast
brush teeth

Compared to your hand example?
exercises.explanation: Every step appears in the right order. Check passes.

exercises.prompt:
Suppose the output came out:

brush teeth
wake up
eat breakfast

What went wrong?
options: The print lines were written in the wrong order
print was used too few times
exercises.explanation: All three steps are there, but out of order. The fix is to reorder the print lines.

exercises.prompt:
Review: how many lines does this show?

print("wake up")
print("eat breakfast")
print("brush teeth")
exercises.explanation: Each print makes its own line, so three prints give three lines. You remembered that from Unit 1!
